questions.question: Is ground-fault protection required for a 2000 A, 208 V service?
questions.answer: No. Ground-fault protection of equipment for solidly grounded services is mandated only on services rated 1000 A or more at more than 150 V to ground (e.g., 347/600 V). A 208 V (120 V to ground) service does not exceed 150 V to ground, so it is not required.
solution_steps: Rule 14-102 requires GFP on solidly grounded services 1000 A and larger that are over 150 V to ground.
208Y/120 V is only 120 V to ground — at or below 150 V — so GFP is not required regardless of the 2000 A rating.

questions.question: What size of overcurrent protection is needed to protect an equipment wire, size #16 AWG?
questions.answer: Both 15 A or 20 A (a #16 AWG equipment wire may be protected at 15 A or, under the permitted conditions, at 20 A)
solution_steps: Overcurrent protection for small/equipment wire is set by Rule 14-104 and Table 13.
For #16 AWG equipment wire the permitted overcurrent device is 15 A or 20 A.

questions.question: For space-heating installations, what type of fuses must be used?
questions.answer: Type D or Type P fuses (time-delay type fuses suitable for the inductive/seasonal load characteristics of space heating)
solution_steps: Space-heating circuits use time-delay fuses to handle inrush/cycling.
The source specifies Type D or Type P fuses.

questions.question: What is the maximum voltage and current rating of knife switches?
solution_steps: Knife switches are limited by the Code to a maximum rating of 750 V and 600 A.

questions.question: Is ground-fault protection required for a circuit at 110 V and rated at 2500 amps?
questions.answer: No. Although the current is 1000 A or more, 110 V does not exceed 150 V to ground, so equipment ground-fault protection under Rule 14-102 is not required.
solution_steps: Rule 14-102 GFP applies to solidly grounded systems 1000 A or larger that exceed 150 V to ground.
110 V is below 150 V to ground → GFP not required.

questions.question: What is the maximum interrupting rating of a 480 V, 125 A circuit breaker (unless specifically marked otherwise)?
solution_steps: Unless marked with a higher interrupting capacity, a moulded-case circuit breaker is assumed to have a default interrupting rating of 10,000 A symmetrical.

questions.question: Is ground-fault protection required for an 800 A, 600/347 V, 3-phase, 4-wire service?
questions.answer: No. The system voltage to ground (347 V) exceeds 150 V, but the service is rated 800 A — below the 1000 A threshold of Rule 14-102 — so equipment ground-fault protection is not required.
solution_steps: Rule 14-102 requires GFP only where the service is 1000 A or more AND over 150 V to ground.
347 V to ground exceeds 150 V, but 800 A is less than 1000 A, so GFP is not mandated.

questions.question: What is the maximum rating of a plug fuse?
solution_steps: Plug fuses (Type T / Type S) are limited to a maximum rating of 30 A.

questions.question: A three-conductor 3/0 copper TW75 cable is installed to supply a 200 A non-continuous load. Determine the maximum size of circuit breaker permitted for this installation.
questions.answer: 200 A. The 3/0 Cu TW75 conductor ampacity (Table 2) is 200 A; for a non-continuous load the overcurrent device is sized to the conductor ampacity, so the maximum breaker is 200 A.
solution_steps: From Table 2, 3/0 AWG copper at 75°C (TW75) has an ampacity of 200 A.
For a non-continuous load, the overcurrent device may be sized at the conductor ampacity (Rule 14-104).
Maximum permitted circuit breaker = 200 A.

questions.question: What must be the rating of general-use switches controlling incandescent lighting in public assembly areas?
questions.answer: They must be "T"-rated (tungsten-rated) general-use switches, because incandescent (tungsten-filament) lamps draw high inrush current.
solution_steps: Incandescent/tungsten lamps have high inrush; switches controlling them must be rated for tungsten loads.
Such switches carry a 'T' rating.

questions.question: According to the requirement, what is the maximum permitted clearing time when a ground-fault current of 3000 A or higher occurs?
questions.answer: 1.0 second (ground-fault protection must clear a ground-fault current of 3000 A or more within a maximum of 1 second)
solution_steps: Equipment ground-fault protection systems have a maximum permitted clearing (operating) time.
For a ground-fault current of 3000 A or higher, the maximum clearing time is 1.0 second.
